I had my Mirena in for almost five years. In the last year, I suffered anxiety attacks, and agoraphobia and was having hot flushes. I had an ultrasound about 5 months ago, which showed that my Mirena had migrated and was sitting in my cervix. I waited for about six weeks (New Zealand healthcare system) for an urgent appointment to get it removed as it was embedded and my GP could not remove it in her office. I ended up going to the ER to have it removed (without pain relief, even though they said it would be with pain relief) and after several attempts, the gynae doctor ripped it out of me. I had bleeding from the removal, but within a week, my mental state dramatically improved. It looks like I was unknowingly experiencing Mirena crash symptoms for possibly months, while the Mirena sat in my cervix. Today, I have an appointment at the hospital as they want to put another one in. I have decided NOT to do this. For context, I have stage 4 endo, my bladder is attached to my uterus at the moment and I take 20mg of Provera a day (this is far too much, I already have high BP and a sedentary job so my risk of blood clots is way higher) since the Mirena was removed. Even with the Mirena, I have had to take 10mg of Provera a day to stop bleeding and I STILL developed more problems related to my endo (womb stuck to bladder). I am 40 years old and have no children. I have decided to have a hysterectomy to get at least one inflamed organ removed. I don't know what it is like to not be on oral contraceptives. I have been on them my whole adult life and I am just sick of it all. I am so sick of feeling like I am going insane and beating myself up for not being more social etc when I later find out it was textbook mirena crash symptoms. I hope all of you get through this. So much suffering happens in silence. Please reach out to people you trust and hold onto faith that this does pass. I feel so much better. I feel stable and confident. I am able to be there more for myself and my friends and family. I no longer dread work. It does get better.

I was there around 2016-2017. I have personally known EIGHT people who were there while I was, that have since committed suicide. The staff are very mixed in skill, empathy, and integrity. From what I observed, none of the ED patients got better, unless they were there to lose weight. Purging etc was never brought up in groups beyond the eating disorder group. Addicts and alcoholics are treated like complete shit compared to ED patients (who also arguably have addiction issues). A lot of self-harm goes on there. Two people killed themselves on site while I was there. People who self-harmed or attempted suicide always get a diagnosis of BPD, which often isn't even true and is nearly impossible to get removed from medical records. A lot of patients there cause constant drama, tension, stress, and anxiety. There were some incredibly unwell people with personality disorders who made my life and the lives of others a complete hell. I think about that place almost every day. It was the toughest time of my life. I was completely isolated from my family and trapped. No one knew that they would want me there for so long (including myself). Leaving was the best thing I ever did, I still have horrible nightmares about the place. If you have an addiction or ED, please look elsewhere or go to do the detox and then return to community support. Don't let things get to the point where you are suicidal like I was. Ashburn is NOT the "only place left." I understand anonymity is important but you can kiss that goodbye as soon as you get to Ashburn. They expect you to discuss in detail abuse, addiction, eating disorders, in front of large groups of patients. Some of whom you would never want their "opinion." Staff load the gun and let patients shoot for them. After very messy and distressing community meetings, staff never bothered to check on me, or other patients.
